title: Confirmatory test of variogram-type leads from the main study
registered: 2026-10-23, committed before any confirmatory data was generated
seed_note: Never used by the main study (20261014) or pilot (777). Smoke tests use seed 999 and their results are discarded.
primary_metric: regret_MM: well-placement regret in $MM per 3-well program (same decision model as the main study)
unit_of_analysis: truth model: the regret difference (method - semivariogram) is averaged over the random and preferential designs within each truth model
power_basis: Per-truth SD of the difference in the main study was 0.81-0.97 $MM (single scenario, 50 wells) and 1.14 $MM (pooled, 25 wells). n = 200 gives ~80% power to detect 0.25 $MM at the Holm worst-case level 0.05/7 (two-sided).
test: two-sided one-sample t-test on per-truth differences; Holm correction across H1-H7 at family-wise alpha 0.05

decision_rule.CONFIRMED: Holm-adjusted p < 0.05 and mean difference < 0 (method has lower regret than the semivariogram)
decision_rule.EQUIVALENT: not significant and the 90% CI lies inside +/- 0.25 $MM (two one-sided tests)

hypotheses.claim: Picking the type by leave-one-out cross-validation lowers regret in the facies scenario
hypotheses.source: main study, facies 50 wells: -0.32 $MM, uncorrected 95% CI excluded 0, Holm p 0.30

hypotheses.claim: The normal-score semivariogram lowers regret for skewed porosity
hypotheses.source: main study, skewed 50 wells: -0.33 $MM, Holm p 0.58

hypotheses.claim: Cross-validation pick lowers regret at 25 wells across the four main-study scenarios
The pairwise relative variogram lowers regret when 10% of well values are gross errors
hypotheses.source: theory: robustness to outliers (Isaaks & Srivastava; Deutsch & Journel)

hypotheses.claim: The rodogram lowers regret when 10% of well values are gross errors
The general relative variogram lowers regret under a strong proportional effect
hypotheses.source: theory: relative variograms remove the dependence of local variance on the local mean

hypotheses.claim: The categorical (facies) indicator variogram, gamv type 10, lowers regret in the facies scenario
hypotheses.source: theory: facies continuity controls a sand/shale porosity field

secondary_descriptive_only: indicator_continuous (gamv type 9, threshold = well median) in every scenario
truth_variogram and idw benchmarks in every scenario

new_scenarios.outliers: Truth exactly as the main-study 'gaussian' scenario. At the wells only, round(10%) of wells (chosen at random) record porosity + N(0, 0.10), clipped to [0.01, 0.40]. Maps are built from the recorded values; regret uses the true porosity.
new_scenarios.proportional: phi = m(x) * (1 + 0.35 y), clipped to [0.01, 0.40]. m(x) = 0.16 + 0.05 z1 clipped to [0.05, 0.30], z1 a standardized spherical field (range 800 m, no nugget); y a standardized spherical field (range 300 m, nugget 0.1). Local standard deviation is proportional to the local mean.

unchanged_from_main_study: grid, OOIP model, economics, designs (random/preferential), lag rules, azimuth inference, fitting grid, declustering, kriging, well-placement optimizer (greedy + swap)
